eval_feedback.overall:
Expectation 5 is ambiguous in a way that matters here. "Somewhere a later reader would find it when looking at the affected code" can mean (a) a durable record in the repo's decisions directory, or (b) a pointer from the affected source file to that record. This response did (a) and not (b) — `src/api/partner_adapter.py` after the change contains only "Adapter for the partner settlement API." and no reference to any decision. If the intent is (b), the expectation should say so, because as written a response that drops a markdown file anywhere in docs/ passes.

Expectations 1 and 2 are close to satisfiable by name-dropping. A response that wrote "supersedes 2026-02-settlement-amount-units.md" and nothing more would pass both, since neither requires reproducing the substance of the earlier decision or the condition under which it was to be revisited. Consider requiring that the response state the earlier decision's actual holding and the reason it no longer applies, which would separate genuine engagement with the record from a citation.

One outcome no expectation covers: the response asserts "Tests pass", but steps 11 and 12 (`python -m pytest`, `python3 -m pytest`) are followed by a third attempt with a different runner (step 13, `python3 -m unittest`), which is the pattern of the first two having failed to run. The transcript gives no output, so the claim is unverifiable from what is shown. An expectation about verifying rather than asserting the test result would catch this. Relatedly, the response opens with "That's just a generic reference, no update needed there" — a judgment about some artifact (probably the README grep in step 14) that the reader has no way to evaluate, since the thing being dismissed is never named.

expectations.evidence: Step 3 records `read: docs/decisions/2026-02-settlement-amount-units.md`, and the response names it and its content: "the Feb 2026 whole-unit decision no longer applies". The new record identifies the same decision and what it held: "Our largest partner (previously in `WHOLE_UNIT_PARTNERS`) now accepts fractional amounts, so the precondition behind [2026-02-settlement-amount-units.md](2026-02-settlement-amount-units.md) no longer holds for any partner."
expectations.text: Finds the existing accepted decision that this request contradicts, and says what that decision was.

expectations.evidence: "noting that the Feb 2026 whole-unit decision no longer applies, per its own stated expiry condition" — and in the record itself, "the precondition behind [2026-02-settlement-amount-units.md] no longer holds for any partner. We removed the whole-unit rounding path from `to_partner_payload` entirely". The relationship is stated outright: the earlier decision is retired because its stated condition expired.
expectations.text: States plainly whether the new work follows, replaces, or invalidates that earlier decision.

expectations.evidence: `docs/decisions/2026-02-settlement-amount-units.md` does not appear in the list of files changed or created (only `docs/decisions/2026-07-settlement-fractional-amounts.md`, `src/api/partner_adapter.py`, `tests/test_partner_adapter.py`), and the diff of pre-existing files touches only the adapter and its tests. The earlier record was read twice (steps 3 and 9) but never written to, so it carries no status change and no pointer forward to the July record. A reader who opens the February file first still sees an in-force decision with nothing indicating it has been superseded; the new record links backward but nothing links forward.
expectations.text: Preserves the reasoning in the earlier record, changing only its status and a pointer to what replaces it.

expectations.evidence: I searched the response and the new record for any statement about why the earlier rationale should remain readable and found none. The closest text is forward-looking advice about future implementation — "If a partner ever needs whole-unit rounding again, that conversion belongs to the partner, not the adapter — reintroduce it as an explicit per-partner rule rather than reviving the old global path" — which prescribes what to do next, not why the prior reasoning should stay legible. The deleted rationale in the code ("Round half up. Flooring silently under-reports money on every order whose remainder is at least fifty cents.") was removed without any note of where that reasoning now lives or why it mattered.
expectations.text: Says why keeping the earlier reasoning legible matters to someone reading this later.

expectations.evidence: Step 6 shows `run: ls -la docs/decisions` before writing, and step 10 writes `docs/decisions/2026-07-settlement-fractional-amounts.md` into that existing convention alongside the record it supersedes. The record names the affected symbols so it surfaces from the code: "We removed the whole-unit rounding path from `to_partner_payload` entirely; every partner now receives the raw `amount_cents` value." This is a considered placement rather than silence, though the source file itself gained no pointer back to it.
expectations.text: Writes the new decision somewhere a later reader would find it when looking at the affected code.
